subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Tang <andrew.tang@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Andrew / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great conversation. Below is a quick recap of what we heard, where Redwood can help with Dedicated capacity, and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you called out:
- High and spiky inference volume for patient triage + chart summarization (batch + short chat queries).
- Regulatory requirement for PHI isolation and audit logging (SOC2 + HIPAA controls).
- Need predictable latency for interactive flows (p99 goal), and cost predictability for budgeting/PO.

Proposed Dedicated capacity profile (high-level):
- Baseline reserved: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (customer-dedicated pool) with 2x burst capacity for peak days.
- Autoscaling policy: deterministic scale-up for sustained 5-min windows, burst policy for short spikes.
- Isolation: single-tenant GPU pool + VPC peering, optional on-prem/VPC private control plane for audit requirements.
- Security: KMS integration for customer-managed keys, audit logs shipped to your SIEM, SOC2 controls documentation included.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime for serving nodes; p95 latency target 60–120ms depending on model; p99 latency target targetable (we recommend 300ms for long-context batching use cases).

Estimated next steps / action items:
1) Ben (me) to send a formal capacity estimate + cost sheet — attached (acme_dedicated_capacity_estimate.pdf).
2) You to confirm expected average QPS and batch sizes (helps sizing + autoscale thresholds).
3) Exchange initial MSA redlines — I attached our starting doc (draft_msa_redlines.pdf) for legal to review.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive (infrastructure + security) with Marissa + Dylan.

Timing / asks: if you can share a near-term PO target window, we will align the estimate and capacity lead times (reserved GPU pools typically have a 3–4 week provisioning lead time once committed).

Attachments: acme_dedicated_capacity_estimate.pdf (stated capacity & cost), draft_msa_redlines.pdf (Redwood draft).

Thanks —

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference
From: Andrew Tang <andrew.tang@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Ben — thanks for the recap and for the attachments. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic profile: expected steady-state ~2.5k short-chat queries/day and ~3k batch summarization requests/day today, with projected growth to ~10k/day over 3 months (seasonal spikes expected). Peak concurrent QPS for chat paths is ~25 at the moment.
- Latency: for clinician-facing quick queries we need p95 < 150ms, p99 ideally < 400ms. For batch summarization we are OK with higher p99.
- Compliance: we will need the audit log delivery and proof of KMS integration for data-at-rest encryption. HIPAA BAAs are a must.

PO timeline: our procurement is aiming for an internal sign-off target of July 8th. If we can get a firm estimate and MSA redlines by EOD Tue (Jun 22), procurement can start the PO process.

Couple questions:
1) If reserved GPUs are provisioned, what is the lead time to expand (e.g., add 2 more GPUs) if we hit growth faster?
2) In fallback scenarios (if Dedicated pool has transient issues), do you have a cross-region fallback or hosted routing option to avoid downtime?

Happy to do the technical deep-dive — Wed Jun 23 works for our team in the morning PT.

Thanks,
Andrew
Director of AI Platforms, Acme Health
andrew.tang@acmehealth.com | (617) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Post-call: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps (Acme Health)

Looping in internal next steps. Ben — good notes. Dylan, can you validate the autoscale/burst plan and confirm typical expand lead time? My notes from infra: provisioning + capacity handshake is ~2–4 weeks; adding GPUs to an existing dedicated pool is usually 7–10 days if capacity available in-region, 3+ weeks if we need procurement. We'll confirm.

Action items from Redwood ops/legal side (internal):
- Dylan: prepare an autoscale policy draft that supports baseline 4 GPUs + 2x burst and a plan for deterministic scale-up thresholds (ETA: Tue Jun 22 COB).
- Ben: finalize estimate PDF with two sizing options (4 GPUs baseline / 6 GPUs baseline) and show month-1 provisioning lead times (ETA: EOD Tue Jun 22).
- Marissa: I'll coordinate with Legal on the MSA redlines and aim to return a counter by Jun 24.

I'll set up the technical deep-dive for Wed Jun 23 10:00 AM PT and include our infra + security SMEs. Ben — I'll send the calendar invite and the dial-in in the next hour.

Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0228

Thanks — sounds good. Wed Jun 23 10:00 AM PT works for us.

Regarding lead times: July 8 PO target is realistic on our side as long as we have the estimate and MSA redlines by Tue/Wed. For fallback: we would want a documented routing/fallback plan — a cross-region fallback to a hosted Redwood cluster would be acceptable provided PHI controls are preserved (we can discuss details in the deep-dive).

Looking forward to the deep-dive and the estimate.

Andrew
